discussion.author: phernandez
discussion.body:
Thanks for the report and the patch.

We're going to keep the `uvx` launcher. A running MCP server imports from the environment it started in; removing uv's cache while the server runs is the same as deleting a virtualenv out from under a running Python process, and any Python tool breaks that way. Switching to a separately installed `basic-memory` executable doesn't remove that dependency, it moves it to a different environment, and it adds an install step `uvx` exists to avoid.

If the cache is being cleared by something other than a manual `uv cache clean` during a session, for example a tool or OS cleanup job, please open an issue with the details and we'll look at how to document or guard against it.

records.title: fix(linux): repair disabled session bus in daemon and PTY environments

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
Rebased onto current `main` (now at `122b8c25d`, "fix(terminal): let Linux IMEs keep the candidate key for a preedit they own (#22607)") to clear the conflict.

The branch was rebuilt on the new base rather than replayed, so the commit SHAs changed and the four commits are now two. #19430 moved the daemon launch out of `daemon-launched-child.ts` into `daemon-launched-child-spawn.ts`, so the repair now sits on `daemonEnv` there, in the new structure. That env feeds both the direct fork and the new `systemd-run --user --scope` arm. `spawn-environment.ts` was hand-applied on top of the #19512 changes. No logic changes to the repair itself.

One thing worth flagging from the rebase: with the marker left in place, `systemd-run --user` itself fails. On a systemd 255 host, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=disabled: systemd-run --user --scope --collect true` exits 1 with "Failed to connect to bus: Connection refused", while the same command without the variable works. So under headless serve the durable-scope launch from #19430 falls back to the unscoped path. The legacy migration and the scope death watch already clear this variable, but `buildDurableDaemonScopeCommand` does not. Because this PR repairs `daemonEnv` before it reaches that builder, it covers that arm too.

Validated locally: the related suites pass (`dbus-session-bus-env`, `daemon-launched-child-spawn`, `daemon-launched-child-identity`, `daemon-cgroup-scope`, 37 tests), the node typecheck is clean, and oxlint is clean on the changed files. Mergeable again.

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
Rebased onto current `main` at `0b2dd0a99b` (v1.4.214-122-g0b2dd0a99b, "fix(runtime): let the phone end a terminal stream by the request that opened it (#23006)") to clear the new conflicts.

Two conflicts, both from changes that landed next to ours:

- `local-pty-spawn-environment.ts`: #22717 added `stripPiProcessOwnerEnv`. Both imports and both calls are kept, with the bus repair still running after the AppImage env cleanup.
- `pty-subprocess/spawn-environment.ts`: `main` now has its own docstring on `createDaemonPtyEnvironment`, so I kept that one and dropped the docstring this branch had added. The Windows test-guard commit now only touches tests.

The import in `dbus-session-bus-env.ts` is also reformatted to match the current oxfmt config.

Checks after the rebase, on Linux arm64:

- The four session-bus suites pass: `dbus-session-bus-env`, `dbus-session-bus-env-wiring`, `daemon-launched-child-spawn` and `daemon-cgroup-scope`.
- Across `src/main/{daemon,providers,pty}`, the branch fails the same 14 files as a clean `main` checkout on this host (native `node-pty` and Windows-only suites, since deps were installed with `--ignore-scripts`). There are no new failures, and the branch adds 12 passing tests.
- `typecheck:node`, oxlint and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.

Still reproduces on v1.4.215 headless `serve`. Shells spawned by the runtime inherit `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=disabled:`, and at startup the daemon logs `durable cgroup-scope launch failed, retrying without cgroup isolation` after `Failed to connect to bus: Connection refused`. That is the `systemd-run --user --scope` path this PR also repairs. A full end-to-end `serve` run from a build of this branch is still not done.

discussion.body: Closing as superseded by #26306, whose session-bus fix was incorporated into #26483. Issue #21119 is already closed as completed. records.title: fix(doctor): validate model-provider plugins through the providers registry

discussion.author: Enough1122
discussion.body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference, author can ignore or act on any point.

**fix(doctor): validate model-provider plugins through the providers registry**

1. The recording wrapper works because the plugin module binds `register_provider` while the patch is active — good. But the validation only observes *module-level* calls; a plugin that registers lazily (inside a function/CLI entry point) is reported as "registered no ProviderProfile" even though it may work at runtime. Since the model-provider contract does require module-level registration, make the error message state that explicitly ("must call providers.register_provider(...) at module level") so plugin authors are not misled.
2. The `finally` block restores `_REGISTRY`/`_ALIASES` from the pre-run snapshot. If the plugin's import chain triggers `_discover_providers()` (e.g. a plugin calls `list_providers()`), bundled providers discovered mid-import are wiped by the restore. Discovery is idempotent so the next `list_providers()` re-populates, but the in-process registry briefly diverges from what other modules may hold; consider restoring only entries that existed before (additive restore) rather than clear+replace.
3. `providers_module._PROVIDER_LIST_CACHE` is snapshotted by direct attribute access — if the attribute name or shape ever changes in `providers/__init__.py`, doctor crashes instead of degrading gracefully. A `getattr` with a fallback would keep the doctor resilient to internal provider-module refactors.
4. Test coverage is solid (accepts, rejects-nothing, warns-on-declared-tools, restores registry). One gap: no test for a `kind: model-provider` plugin that actually registers tools/hooks at module level (the warning path is only exercised via the `provides_tools` manifest declaration, not real registration).

discussion.body: @oliver-mee you had this right first — `doctor` was pushing `kind: model-provider` plugins through `_load_plugin` and failing every valid one on the missing `register(ctx)`. #117451 lands the same fix (imports through `providers._import_plugin_dir`, the real discovery loader, then restores the registry) with you credited as co-author on that commit. **Approach is sound.** Restoring vendor casing *after* title-casing (a `VENDOR_CASING` allow-list + a `PARAMETER_COUNT` regex) keeps the pipeline a single normalized pass and cleanly covers the issue's top wrong-token table: `Deepseek→DeepSeek`, `Glm→GLM`, `Minimax→MiniMax`, `Openai→OpenAI`, `Mimo→MiMo`, plus `8b→8B` / `a3b→A3B` via `/\b(a?)(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)b\b/gi`. Good catch also fixing the `gemini-` branch, which was the one path that returned before any capitalisation (`gemini-2.5-pro` → "Gemini 2.5 pro"); it now title-cases like the others. Test coverage in both `model-status-label.test.ts` and `model-menu-panel.test.tsx` matches the issue's examples, and checks are green.

**Residuals (non-blocking), for awareness:**
- `VENDOR_CASING` is a curated allow-list, so the long tail from the issue's 1093-casing-diff analysis (vendors beyond the ~11 mapped) still title-cases and will need map additions over time. That's a fine, maintainable scope for the frequent cases — just noting it won't be exhaustive.
- `/\bIt\b/→IT` and `/\bAi\b/→AI` are broad word-level rules. They're aimed at the `-it` (instruction-tuned) and `-ai` suffixes and are low-risk since model ids rarely carry the English words "it"/"ai" as standalone tokens, but a vendor/model literally named "Ai"/"It" would be upper-cased. Acceptable given the token frequency, worth a glance if a future model id trips it.

Reads correct and well-covered to me for #85849.

discussion.author: Enough1122
discussion.body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference, author can ignore or act on any point.

**fix(desktop): keep vendor casing in model display names**

Restoring vendor casing after title-casing is a clean single-pass design, and fixing the `gemini-` branch (the one path that skipped title-casing) is a good catch. Tests cover the issue's examples. A few observations:

1. `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-status-label.ts:164-167` — `/\bIt\b/ → 'IT'` and `/\bAi\b/ → 'AI'` are broad word-level rules. They're aimed at `-it`/`-ai` suffix tokens and are low-risk today, but any future model id carrying the standalone English words "it"/"ai" (or a vendor literally named "Ai") would be upper-cased. Consider anchoring these to suffix position (e.g. `\bit\b$` after the variant strip) if a collision ever appears.
2. `model-status-label.ts:172` — `PARAMETER_COUNT` runs with the `i` flag after title-casing, so already-cased tokens like "32B" are re-matched and re-written identically (harmless). Worth noting the `a?` prefix also matches a bare leading "a" — no current id trips it, but a hypothetical "3ab"-style token would produce "3AB". Very low risk.
3. `VENDOR_CASING` is a curated allow-list, so the long tail of vendors (the issue's 1093-casing-diff analysis) will keep title-casing and need map additions over time. Fine scope for the frequent cases, just noting it won't be exhaustive — a follow-up could generate the map from the catalog's provider display names.

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
Added runtime proof to the PR body: this branch built, its CLI listing all fourteen restored rows with `qwen3-coder-next` gone, and a completion running end to end through `qwen-token-plan/deepseek-v4-pro`, which is a row this PR restores and which cannot be selected on current `main` at all. Nothing here is more stale than what users have today, and keeping it a pure revert is what makes the diff reviewable as one decision. #113579 then rebases on top and corrects the three ceilings with boundary-probe evidence.

That said, the review is right that the two should not land as contradictory catalog states, and I would rather solve the shape than argue about it.

@steipete, this is really a question for you, because there are three open PRs against the same catalog and the sensible grouping depends on what you want to own:

1. **#118726 (this one)** restores the catalog to the published fourteen.
2. **#113579** corrects three output ceilings and adds video input, measured on the live gateway.
3. **#113578** adds `qwen3.8-max-preview` with an always-thinking effort contract. This one is already at `proof: sufficient` and `ready for maintainer look`.

I am happy to fold #113579 into this PR so the catalog lands correct in one change, which is what the review's own recommendation ("restore every documented chat model with verified metadata") points at. Say the word and I will do that and close #113579 as superseded.

I would suggest keeping #113578 separate regardless. It carries a real code change to the thinking contract rather than catalog metadata, and it has already cleared contributor-side review; folding it in would drag a finished PR back into an open one.

Two things I would rather flag than quietly bundle:

- The video modality in #113579 is where the outstanding China-region question actually attaches. If I fold that PR in, I would suggest taking the three `max_tokens` corrections and leaving video for a follow-up, so an unresolved regional argument cannot block ceilings that are proven by boundary probes.
- The gateway now also serves `qwen3.8-max` and `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, neither of which is in any catalog yet. Correcting myself from an earlier draft of this comment: I do have measured metadata for both. `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` is a dated snapshot of `deepseek-v4-flash` (0731 being 31 July), and `qwen3.8-max` is the GA of `qwen3.8-max-preview`, whose ceiling I have just reconfirmed on the GA id: `max_tokens=131072` accepted, `131073` rejected with `Range of max_tokens should be [1, 131072]`, identical to the preview. They stay out of this PR because it is a revert, not because the numbers are unknown. Happy to add them in a follow-up.

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
On the remaining finding, that this applies Global-only evidence to the China endpoint: here is China endpoint evidence.

I listed both Token Plan endpoints today. They serve an identical catalogue:

```console
# Global, ap-southeast-1
$ curl -s $GLOBAL_BASE/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-sp-<redacted>" | jq -r '.data[].id' | sort
# 22 ids

# China, cn-beijing
$ curl -s $CN_BASE/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-sp-<redacted>" | jq -r '.data[].id' | sort
# 22 ids, byte-identical to the Global list
```

Concretely, for this PR:

- All fourteen restored models are present on the China endpoint. None is missing.
- `qwen3-coder-next` is absent from China as well, so removing it is correct for both endpoints rather than only for Global.
- The two lists are identical, so this branch advertises nothing to China users that the China endpoint does not serve.

That covers the model IDs, which is the part of the finding about advertising unsupported rows.

On the output ceilings I want to be precise about what is measurement and what is reasoning, because this PR has been held to a high evidence bar and I would rather not blur that line now.

The measurement is the identical catalogue above. The reasoning is that these are the same models: Token Plan is one product offered in two regions, the two endpoints serve the same twenty-two model IDs, and an output ceiling is a property of the model build rather than of the region it is served from. `kimi-k2.7-code` on cn-beijing is the same `kimi-k2.7-code` as on ap-southeast-1. There is no mechanism by which the same model would carry a different output cap on the other endpoint, and no vendor documentation describes one.

I cannot turn that into a China completion transcript, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise: my China Token Plan subscription is lapsed. A lapsed subscription still lists the full catalogue but denies every completion, which is why I can show you the China model list above but not a China request. That is also worth knowing as a general trap on this service, since it means list length alone never proves entitlement.

Two things that limit the risk if you would still rather not take the inference:

- **This PR does not widen the coupling.** `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_MODEL_CATALOG` has been one shared array since the provider landed; `buildQwenTokenPlanProvider` swaps only the base URL. The ceilings this branch corrects were themselves shared and were never China-proven either. Splitting the catalog by region is a reasonable design change, but it is a pre-existing design question rather than something this branch introduces.
- **A wrong ceiling fails loudly, not silently.** The gateway rejects an over-limit request with `400 Range of max_tokens should be [1, N]`, naming the enforced range. It does not truncate or misbehave quietly.

If you would prefer the region split regardless, I am happy to do it: `resolveQwenTokenPlanBaseUrl` already selects the endpoint, so a per-region catalog is a contained change and I can send it as a follow-up. I would just rather not hold the restoration behind it, because today every China user is looking at the same six-row picker with a model that 404s on their endpoint too.

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
Correction to my previous comment: the video modality is out, reverted in `8a5abbcf`. CI caught something I had not known about.

`test/scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.ts` fails on every row that declares video with `Invalid option: expected one of "text"|"image"|"document"`. The two schemas disagree:

- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.ts:48` types `input` as `"text" | "image" | "audio" | "video" | "document"`, which is why it typechecks and the extension tests pass.
- `packages/model-catalog-core/src/remote-catalog-bundle.ts:49` narrows the published bundle to `["text", "image", "document"]`, and that is what the publish script validates the manifest against.

So a video-capable model cannot declare it in a shipped catalog today, whatever the gateway does. Six Token Plan models do accept video input, but that is not expressible here, so it is dropped rather than worked around. Widening the bundle schema is a reasonable thing to want but it is not a catalog restore, and I would rather raise it separately than slip it into this PR. Happy to open that as its own issue if you would find it useful.

What remains from #113579 is the `(Team Edition)` docs scrub, which stands: Personal and Team are separate editions sharing one endpoint, so the old label described the wrong axis.

The rest of the PR is unchanged: the restored 14 rows, the three corrected ceilings, and `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`. Local checks after the revert are 79 passing across the three provider test files, plus `publish-model-catalog.test.ts` 8 passing, which is the lane that failed.

discussion.author: oliver-mee

records.title: [Bug]: Headless browser pages intermittently return empty screenshots

discussion.author: AmethystLiang
discussion.body: Thanks for reporting. Looking into it

discussion.author: jonathanelmgren
discussion.body:
Same failure on the packaged release, and on our machine it is not intermittent.

**Setup:** Orca 1.4.219 (Electron 43.7.5), Linux x64, `orca serve` as a systemd user service with the Xvfb display (`:99`) that Orca starts itself. No desktop window.

**Observed:** for a tab created with `orca tab create --url https://example.com`:

- the first `orca screenshot` returns a 1x1 PNG;
- every later screenshot is 1280x773 but holds only the page's root background colour: no text and no boxes. 6 of 6 retries after a reload were identical (4560 bytes). After `document.documentElement.style.background = 'red'`, the screenshot is solid red and the injected content is still missing. So the capture reaches the live page, but the page's layers are never drawn;
- `orca snapshot` and `orca exec "eval ..."` work normally;
- the GPU process logs `x11_software_bitmap_presenter.cc:147] XGetWindowAttributes failed for window <id>` once for each tab window created.

**Reproduced outside Orca** with the same Electron binary, a fresh Xvfb, `app.disableHardwareAcceleration()` + `--disable-gpu` (as `_4i()` does in serve mode), and a `BrowserWindow({show:false, width:1280, height:800})` loading example.com. Five captures in a row per mode:

| mode | results |
|---|---|
| hidden window, CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` with Orca's kick loop (`invalidate()` + 1x1-clip JPEG captures at 250/750/1750/3750 ms) | 1x1, good, background-only, good, background-only |
| hidden window, CDP without kicks | timeout, good, timeout, good, timeout |
| hidden window, `webContents.capturePage()` | partial, then good x4 |
| `webPreferences.offscreen: true` | good x5 |
| `win.showInactive()` on the Xvfb display | good x5 |

So the kick workaround in the capture path does not just fail to force a frame. On the first call, the main request resolves with the kick's 1x1 frame; after that, it often resolves with an empty frame that has only the background colour. Like the original report, enabling offscreen rendering for serve-mode tabs fixed it every time here. Mapping the window with `showInactive()` on the private Xvfb display also works.

Minor, seen while testing: `orca screenshot --format jpeg` returns a PNG.

records.title: OpenCode 2.x sessions are not indexed (session_v2 / session_message tables)

discussion.author: Dicklesworthstone
discussion.body:
Thanks for the precise report. Confirmed from the code: the OpenCode connector in `franken_agent_detection` (which cass uses to find and parse OpenCode sessions) reads only the 1.x `session`/`message` tables. Nothing on its current main references `session_v2` or `session_message`, so a session that exists only in the 2.x tables is never indexed, as you describe. Tracked as bead `coding_agent_session_search-9su4d`.

Plan:
- Read `session_v2`/`session_message` when they exist, alongside the 1.x tables.
- De-duplicate migrated sessions by id and prefer the `session_v2` row.
- Map each message `type` and its `data` from OpenCode 2.x's own source, not only the user `{text}` shape. Sub-agent sessions (`parent_id`) get the same treatment as on the 1.x path, and non-message events such as `idle` or `agent-switched` don't become empty messages.

The fix ships as a `franken_agent_detection` release plus a cass pin bump. I'll follow up here when a build with it is available.

discussion.author: Dicklesworthstone
discussion.body:
Fixed in `franken-agent-detection` 0.3.3 (released today; fix commit 7f4c2dd), which cass now pins on `main` (6d75777e).

The connector now reads `session_v2`/`session_message` alongside the 1.x tables:
- A session migrated from 1.x is indexed once, with its 2.x title and transcript.
- 2.x rows follow `seq`.
- Assistant turns keep their text, reasoning and tool text results, credited to the model id.
- `idle` and the `*-switched` events add no messages.
- Later 2.x builds that keep 2.x sessions in `session` itself are read the same way.

End-to-end check with your repro, using release binaries:
- An isolated HOME held an OpenCode 2.0.16-shaped `opencode.db` with a v2-only session and a session migrated from 1.x. The 1.x tables kept one stale message that the 2.x transcript no longer has.
- Each binary ran `cass index`, then `cass search '<phrase>' --agent opencode --robot --mode lexical`.

| phrase | where it lives | cass on FAD 0.3.2 (`main` before, 03a25ad1) | cass on FAD 0.3.3 (patch-identical to 6d75777e) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `platypusdistinctivephrase` | v2-only session, user turn | 0 hits | 1 hit, "Started on 2.x" |
| `echidnaassistantreply` | v2-only session, assistant turn | 0 hits | 1 hit, "Started on 2.x" |
| `wombatmigratedphrase` | migrated session, 2.x turn | 0 hits | 1 hit, "Migrated to 2.x" |
| `quokkaleftbehind` | migrated session, stale 1.x copy only | 1 hit, "Migrated on 1.x" | 0 hits |

Per the index report, the OpenCode connector went from 1 conversation / 1 message (the stale 1.x copy) to 2 conversations / 3 messages.

It will ship in the next cass release. Until then, a build from `main` has it.

discussion.author: Dicklesworthstone
discussion.body: Shipped in v0.10.0 (https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search/releases/tag/v0.10.0), which pins franken-agent-detection 0.3.3 (6d75777e): OpenCode 2.x `session_v2`/`session_message` sessions are indexed, and a session migrated from 1.x is indexed once. Closing; reopen with a sample if a 2.x session is still missing.

discussion.author: rubensousa-uw
discussion.body:
Another data point, this time on a **release tag**, not just `master`: `v2026.1012.0` (`bba6a45f0`) is affected too, so following the git-ref install docs onto the current stable release fails the same way.

On a clean `git archive` of the tag:

    $ corepack pnpm@9.15.4 install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only
    Scope: all 36 workspace projects
     ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE  Cannot install with "frozen-lockfile" because pnpm-lock.yaml is not up to date with <ROOT>/server/package.json

The `server` importer in the tag's `pnpm-lock.yaml` has no entries for two specifiers that `server/package.json` declares: `"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.30.0"` and `"light-my-request": "^6.6.0"`. Run through `paperclipai install --repo <owner>/<repo> --ref <sha>` (CLI 2026.1005.0), the install stops at `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, 12 s in, before any build.

So the drift is not only a `master` problem between releases: it shipped in a tag, and `install --ref` is the one path that turns it into a hard stop.

On our side the workaround was a lockfile-only commit on top of the tag, generated with the repo's `packageManager` (`corepack pnpm@9.15.4 install --lockfile-only`, +28/−1 lines). After it, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes on a clean tree (27 s). That fixes our fork, but not anyone who installs the tag itself.

+1 to the frozen-first, logged fallback proposed above. A release-time check that `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only` passes on the tag would also catch this before a release ships.

records.title: Model catalog publish rejects video input that the plugin SDK type accepts (regression of #97048 on the hosted-catalog path)
Token Plan catalog curation in #113681 used the Coding Plan endpoint: adds a model that 404s and keeps the oldest of each family

discussion.author: oliver-mee
discussion.body:
Opened #118726 for this.

It reverts the Token Plan portion of #113681 and nothing else: the fourteen published chat models come back, `qwen3-coder-next` goes, and the other providers from that PR plus `QWEN_MODEL_CATALOG` are untouched.

I re-probed the gateway today before filing, and got a cleaner piece of evidence than the original report had. On one key in one session, `qwen3-coder-next` returns `404 Model not exist` while `kimi-k2.7-code`, which is genuinely outside that key's tier, returns `403 Access to model denied`. The two failure modes are distinct, so the 404 is the endpoint not routing the model rather than an entitlement gap on my subscription. The same 404 reproduces on a second key at a different tier.

One correction to my own report while I am here. I said anyone selecting `qwen-token-plan/qwen3-coder-next` from the picker gets a hard 404. That overstated it: the row carries `status: "deprecated"`, and `isPickerVisibleCatalogEntry` in `src/agents/model-catalog-visibility.ts` filters deprecated rows out of the picker, so it is only reachable by typing the exact ref. The nine missing models are the user-visible part; the dead row is mainly evidence of which endpoint the catalog was checked against.
